chunks: And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, only forbade usury so that kindness would not disappear.

key_terms.الرِّبَا: usury; unlawful increase in financial dealings
key_terms.اللَّهُ: Allah, the One who legislates and prohibits
key_terms.الْمَعْرُوفُ: recognized goodness, kindness, and socially virtuous conduct
key_terms.حَرَّمَ: forbade; made unlawful as a divine ruling
key_terms.لِئَلَّا: so that not; indicating the wisdom behind the prohibition

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah forbid usury in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, prohibited usury because it undermines al-maʿrūf, the culture of goodness and benevolence among people. It presents the ban on riba not only as a legal ruling but also as a protection for social virtue and mutual care.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4936 - In the narration of Muhammad ibn Atiyyah from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), he said:
"Indeed, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, only forbade usury so that acts of kindness would not disappear."
